verdict: REVISE BEFORE BUILD. The direction is sound and unusually well grounded: I re-verified the load-bearing code claims against the repo and they hold (AppShell.tsx aside lg:hidden nav card and sticky top-[82px]; me.roles.join(' · ') printing raw role codes; RoleRoute denial -> /submissions; /incidents/:id rendering the list; canEdit gating on the literal FIELD_WORKER; WorkflowTree.tsx + api/workflowTree.ts genuinely dead; no @theme block in index.css; .esri-view isolation-only rule respected; .map-stack-guard and qualityProfile real; list_assessments already accepting office_code; CONSULTED a real assignment_role; /auth/me clearing the token on any failure; LoginPage hard-coding /my-work and min-h-[620px]). The measured baselines match brief-core.md exactly, all 15 walkthrough tasks are carried into Appendix A with the same 'today' counts, and the arithmetic (158 -> 74 clicks, 66 days across 7 phases) is internally consistent. But it is not buildable as written. Four classes of defect block it: (1) an entire persona is unimplemented — the Maintenance Field Reporter has no Home section and no route by which to answer the coordinator's information request, which is the return leg of a flow the plan does specify; (2) several layout numbers cannot fit the plan's own measured content widths (three regions need 1240px inside a measured 1097px main at 1440; the phone map height ignores the 56px bottom nav; /terrain and /map stack two bottom bars); (3) at least four backend dependencies are missing from the B1-B10 list and one of them silently defeats the whole rollout plan — parse_user_metadata whitelists exactly three keys (district, office_code, office_location), so the runtime feature flag cannot be read from /auth/me metadata as §8 states; (4) the primary document is materially thinner than plan.json — five page specs carry no responsive layout and ten carry no empty state, including Terrain and Road Inventory, the two screens with S4 responsive failures. Fix the 24 items below and this becomes a plan a team can execute.
coverageGaps: Maintenance Field Reporter has no Home. §7.2's essential list enumerates grouped sections for coordinator, office chief, branch chief, engineer, reviewer and admin — the reporter is absent — while §4 gives their Home as 'My reports' and §5.5 makes '/' the single home for everyone. What a reporter sees at '/' is undefined in both the markdown and plan.json.

The reporter's third top task, 'answer a request for information' (§4), has no destination. §9.2 writes the copy ('The coordinator needs more information: route, post mile. Update your report to send it back.') and B10 exposes the requested fields, but no screen, route or flow lets the reporter edit and resend. The coordinator's 'Ask the reporter' disposition therefore commits into a dead end.

Not Found has no destination. brief-screens.md:951 specifies it as a real screen with a plain-language explanation the audit lists under 'Strengths to keep'; the plan replaces it with a bare redirect (§5.5: '404 ... navigate here'). No spec, no layout, no copy — and anonymous users hitting a bad URL now chain '*' -> '/' -> ProtectedRoute -> '/login' with no signal that the URL was wrong.

Access Sharing has no destination. brief-screens.md:1141 documents a live, permission-gated surface (user search, Grant read access, Revoke, 'Users with explicit read access (n)', gated on submission.can_manage_permissions). The plan mentions it only as the word 'Share' inside §7.6's Secondary overflow list — no essential/secondary/hidden classification, no layout, no empty state.

The Terrain 'Cross-section statistics' panel (brief-screens.md:1471, rail 'Stats', 15 tiles) has no destination: 'Stats' and 'statistics' appear zero times in the plan. §7.15 relocates Profile, Points and Setup but is silent on this panel, so its fate (merge into Profile per the brief's 'ten of fifteen tiles duplicate the Profile panel', or keep) is undecided.

The session-validation gate (AuthGateLoading, brief-screens.md:904) has no spec. It renders in place of every ProtectedRoute/RoleRoute child and on /login when a token exists; the plan's only adjacent statement is 'skeleton rows first' on Home.

Five page specs in UX_REDESIGN_PLAN.md carry no **Layout** line at all — §7.8 History, §7.13 Records–Assessments, §7.15 Terrain, §7.17 Road inventory, §7.18 Settings — so five screens have no phone/tablet/desktop composition in the primary deliverable. Two of them (Terrain, Road inventory) are exactly the screens §2.4 flags with S4 responsive failures.

Ten page specs carry no **Empty** line in the markdown: §7.1, 7.8, 7.10, 7.11, 7.13, 7.14, 7.15, 7.16, 7.17, 7.18. plan.json supplies them; the two artifacts therefore disagree about what was specified.

Appendix A is a click-count table, not a set of reference journeys. All 15 tasks are present and the 'today' counts match brief-core.md, but no step sequence is given for any of them, so the 'new' counts (19 for the engineer form, 3 for the coordinator map task, 4 for the reviewer decision) are assertions no reader can check against the specs in §7.

print/PDF parity, called out in the agreed research heading for long technical inspection forms (brief-research.md:64), is reduced to the two words 'print CSS' in §8 and §6.2. No spec for printing an approved GISA, which is a routine Caltrans record-keeping need.

The Password Reset dialog (brief-screens.md:39) and the Delete submission dialog (brief-screens.md:1059) survive only as words inside overflow menus ('Reset password in the row overflow', 'Refresh, Delete and Share in the overflow') with no confirm-sheet spec, although P6 requires every such action to sit inside a confirm surface.
contradictions: §6.2 Records list, tablet cell contradicts itself in one sentence: '4 prioritised columns + trailing action ... actions second not last'. The ResponsiveList component row in §8 says 'actions second'. Pick one.

§6.2 Map+list tablet cell says 'lg: side by side, map 1.4fr / list minmax(300px,1fr)' and, in the same cell, 'Rail auto-collapses to 56 px below 1366'. §7.14 repeats it as 'the list rail auto-collapses to 56 px below 1366 px'. Between 1024 and 1365 the list is therefore simultaneously ≥300px and 56px. (56px also collides with the 80px nav rail from §5.3.)

Dialog breakpoint stated three ways: §5.3 (640–767 row) implies centred max-w-xl dialogs from sm; §6.2 says 'Centred panel from sm'; §7.10 says 'full page with a sticky bottom bar below md, centred dialog at md+'. plan.json repeats both. sm and md cannot both be the switch.
§5.3 specifies the iPad rail as 'icon + 10 px label'; §6.3 and §12 forbid essential text below 12px ('Text nodes under 12 px ... 0 for essential text'). Primary navigation labels are essential text.

§6.3 allows exactly one scroll region per screen from a closed list — 'sticky rail, sheet body, dialog body, or a table's horizontal wrapper' — but §6.2, §7.4 and §7.6 add horizontal scroll-snap chip strips (form section index on md, cross-link chip row on the case-file phone header) that are scroll regions and are not on the list. On the phone form-section page a chip strip also coexists with a sticky bottom bar.

§9.3 item 5 prescribes a coach mark whose copy is 'nothing is saved until you press Record decision', but §7.9 Hidden explicitly deletes that control ('the separate \'Record decision · use selected Event Group\' commit') and §7.9 Actions renames the primary to 'Accept and send to North GeoTech Office'. The onboarding copy teaches a button the plan removes.

§9.3 opens 'No welcome tour, coach-mark carousel or video' — correctly sourced to brief-research.md:37 — and then prescribes 'Exactly two coach marks'. The research is cited to reject the mechanic and then the mechanic is adopted without a stated reason for the exception.

§7.4 gives the case file two status chips: the Next-step banner opens with a 'status chip' and the Header carries 'one status chip'. This is the same duplicate-status pattern the plan strips elsewhere (§7.2 hides the rail header as an 'exact duplicate 15 px above'; §7.6 hides 'the status caption that restates the badge').

§4 says the legacy REVIEWER account role 'grants nothing', but SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:161 sets canReview from the literal REVIEWER or ADMIN, and OPERATIONAL_ROLE_NAMES in roleModel.ts includes REVIEWER, so today it grants submission-level Approve/Return plus route access to /event-groups, /assessments and /gis/terrain-cross-sections.
§5.2 heading says 'Phone tab strip: four visible plus More' and then lists three visible plus More (Overview · Who has it · Form · More). §7.4's layout line uses the three-plus-More version.

§9.1 maps Mission Center -> Map and Terrain Cross Section -> 'Terrain profile' under 'one name per object, everywhere', but §5.5 keeps 'Mission Center' as a visible page eyebrow and §5.1/§5.4 label the nav item 'Terrain'. Three visible names survive a section titled one-name-per-object.

Phone card grammar differs between artifacts: UX_REDESIGN_PLAN.md §7.3 says '3-line cards (title + status / location / age)'; plan.json's records-incidents phone layout says line 1 is 'title with the ERIS number muted plus workflow label'. Three facts including 'With North GeoTech Office' will not hold one line at 375px, so the '3 lines' budget is false in the JSON version.

Road Inventory column count differs between artifacts and breaks the budget: §7.17 lists Version, Status, Actions, Rows, Extract date plus desktop-only uploaded date, source file and skipped rows (8 cells), while plan.json says 'Six columns plus Actions' — against P4's and §12's 'no table exceeds ... 6 at xl'.

§5.5 says '/assessments/:id ... One in-page hop through incident_id — no async route resolver', and Appendix B uses 'cannot be statically redirected and needs an async resolver' as the reason to reject nested URLs — yet the same route map redirects /submissions/:id/photo-evidence 'via submission -> incident', which is precisely an async resolve on a legacy deep link.
unsupportedClaims: §12 labels the tap-target baseline 'Targets under 44 px on coarse pointers | 120 · 41 · 17 · 12'. brief-core.md:9 defines smallTapTargets as elements with width or height < 40px. The baseline is a <40px count presented as a <44px count, so the 'reduce to 0' target is measured against a different threshold than the one it claims.
'Load 3D terrain (about 20 MB)' (§6.2, §7.7) states a payload size that appears nowhere in the three briefs and is not measured anywhere in the evidence. It ships as user-facing copy.
'the list rail auto-collapses to 56 px below 1366 px' (§6.2, §7.14): 1366 appears in none of the briefs and no measurement supports that threshold.

'navigator.deviceMemory < 4' as the 3D gate (§6.2, §7.7 via 'disabled with a visible reason'): deviceMemory appears nowhere in brief-research.md and is unimplemented in Safari/iOS, i.e. on the plan's own primary field device, where `undefined < 4` is false and the gate passes.

§7.7 lists 'Open / Download always visible on touch' as a change, but index.css:138-142 already ships `@media (hover: none) { .attachment-tile .attachment-tile-actions { opacity: 1 } }` plus `:focus-within`. The residual risk is the hybrid case (iPad with a trackpad reports hover:hover while the user taps), which the plan does not name.

§6.3's justification 'Tailwind v4 already scopes hover: inside @media (hover:hover), so touch never sees it' does not cover the actual hover affordance in this codebase, which is hand-written CSS in index.css:132 (.attachment-tile:hover), not a Tailwind hover: utility.

B2 is presented as one of only three gating backend items ('Office-scope the APPROVED finalize list'), but list_assessments already accepts office_code (assessments.py:785) and /auth/me already returns metadata.office_code (user_metadata.py:44-48). brief-core.md:560 says the same. This is a one-line client change, not a backend gate — so the headline 'Only three backend items gate' is really two.

Appendix B sources 30+ decisions to 'the new-user judge', 'the field judge', 'the domain judge', 'the engineering judge' and four proposals with numeric scores ('case-file 34.3, task-first 34.5', 'new-user judge 8.8 and domain judge 8.7') without a single file path. The artifacts do exist (scratchpad/ux/design/judge-*.json, proposal-*.json, spec-*.json) and the two-two split is real, but as written no reader can trace any claim, and none of these are among the three agreed briefs.
§1 and §8 assert 'three of four proposals assumed [a feature flag] this repo lacks'. Unverifiable from the briefs, and it is the sole justification for a budget line.
responsiveGaps: Phone map height is wrong by a bar: §6.2 sets the map to calc(100dvh - var(--header-h) - 44px) on a route (/map) that is a top-level nav destination and therefore keeps the 56px bottom nav bar plus env(safe-area-inset-bottom). The bottom ~56-90px of the map sits under the nav bar.

Bars stack on /terrain: §6.3 says bottom nav hides 'on :id routes' and §7.13-style edit/decision pages, but /terrain is an engineer's fourth nav destination, and §7.15 plus plan.json give it 'a three-button bottom action bar' below lg. Nav bar (56) + action bar (44) = the stacked bars the plan forbids; the scene height calc(100dvh - var(--header-h)) subtracts neither.

The desktop three-region form cannot fit the measured viewport. §6.2 specifies index 200-240 | form ≤720 | pane ≥320 = ≥1240px of content plus gaps, and §5.3 puts three regions at xl (1280). brief-core.md measures main at 1097px wide on a 1440 laptop with the 256px sidebar. The composition does not fit at 1280 or at 1440 — only above ~1600.

Two panes at lg (1024) are under-specified for the case file: with the 80px rail plus padding the content is ~896px, so a 300-340px queue leaves ~540px for a detail that §7.4 says must hold banner, key facts, a progress rail beside them and a right-edge supporting pane.

The 640-767 band is left as the phone shell ('Same as phone', §5.3/§6.1) even though the plan's own device list puts 'iPad ½ split (678)' there and brief-research.md:188 recommends a 72-80px rail from 600px. On a device the owner calls primary, a half-screen window gets a phone bottom bar.

§6.2 tablet 'md: 4 prioritised columns' has no truncation or minimum-width rule for the location string ('District 7 · Los Angeles · Route 101 · PM 12.30' is ~45 characters) inside the plan's own ~656px iPad-portrait content width; brief-core.md already records that cells 'wrap heavily' at 661px. P4 also forbids title= carrying information not visible, so the usual truncation escape is closed and no replacement is given.

No acceptance metric protects the fold below the header. mainContentStartsAtPx ≤64/≤120 measures where main begins, not where the case-file tab strip or the primary action lands after a Next-step banner that §7.4 requires to quote a reviewer comment 'in full'. A long comment can push the tab strip off a 375×812 screen while the metric still passes.
§6.3 says the bottom nav hides 'on input focus'. On iPad Safari with a hardware keyboard the visual viewport does not shrink, so navigation would disappear for no reason; no condition is given.
§7.7 leaves the phone composition undecided — 'map (or a Map | Photos control) then a 2-column grid' — for the tab that carries the most content in the product.

100dvh is prescribed for maps and scenes; on iOS Safari dvh changes as the URL bar collapses, resizing the ArcGIS view continuously during scroll. No guard (a resize debounce, or svh for the map container) is specified.
dataMinimalismGaps: Two status chips on the case-file Overview (§7.4 header chip + Next-step banner chip) — the exact duplication the plan removes elsewhere.

§7.17 Road inventory desktop reaches 8 table cells (Version, Status, Actions, Rows, Extract date + uploaded date, source file, skipped rows), over P4's 6-at-xl budget and over the §12 metric; plan.json says 6 + Actions, so neither artifact is inside the budget with the action column counted.

Two raw system names are deliberately kept in visible text: 'GISA · Form #9' as the form eyebrow (§7.6) and 'Mission Center' as the map eyebrow (§5.1, §5.5). §9.1's rule is one name per object, and §9.4 item 11 says codes are demoted into a 'Technical details' disclosure — which is where these belong.
plan.json's records-incidents phone card puts title + muted ERIS number + workflow label on line 1 at 375px (see contradictions); either the line count or the fact count is wrong.

§7.5 'Who has it' essential runs to People + assignment roles + hand-off note + a five-timestamp pipeline + office name + routing reason + override + a forms table + the banner. The phone composition thins it, but no explicit fact budget is stated for the tablet composition, where it is the default tab for /assessments/:id.

§7.2's Home row carries title + location + status badge + 'Waiting on you since 3 days' + muted ids + 'Sent to you by M. Ortiz (Office Chief) 4 h ago — note'. With the hand-off line that is 6 facts against P4's 'max 5 facts per row'; the plan does not say the hand-off line is detail-only.
learnabilityGaps: §9.2 maps only 2 of the 8 workflow-tree node statuses. workflow_tree.py:26-33 defines COMPLETED, CURRENT, PENDING, WAITING_ON_REPORTER, REVISION_REQUESTED, SKIPPED, TERMINAL, UNASSIGNED; the table covers UNASSIGNED and SKIPPED. ProgressRail mounts that contract in Phase 2, so six codes would render unmapped and fail Phase 0's own 'zero raw codes' CI gate.

The plan and the backend disagree on the reporter's job title. §9.1 sets 'Maintenance Field Reporter'; workflow_tree.py:40 _ROLE_TITLES already renders 'Maintenance Field Worker' in the tree the plan mounts. Two names for one role in one screen — the defect §9 exists to close.

'Event Group' is kept as a primary label despite being the highest-confusion term in §2.5 and the term that blocks the coordinator at step 1. The mitigation is a first-use definition; no plainer alternative is proposed or rejected on the record.

Onboarding relies on per-account state that has nowhere to live: 'once per account' (§9.3 items 1 and 5), 'dismissal is remembered per account' (§9.4 item 10), the Records-assessments 'dismissible first-visit hint' and the 60-day return card. §7.18 says theme and density are 'Stored in this browser only' and open question 8 concedes there is no user record for preferences. On shared field iPads these all misfire.
The coach-mark copy teaches a deleted control (see contradictions).
The reporter, the one persona who is not a trained operational user, gets the least specification: no Home group, no answer-the-request flow, no next-step copy of their own beyond one row in §9.2.

§9.3 item 4 makes 'every status chip tap-to-open', while §6.2 makes the phone list card 'one ≥64 px link'. A tappable popover trigger nested inside a full-card link is ambiguous to tap and invalid to nest; no resolution is given (row-level info button, or chip only on detail pages).

§7.6 keeps the word 'GISA' in the eyebrow for veterans while §4 lists 'the words GISA and REJECTED' under what the engineer is never burdened with. The exemption is reasonable but the two statements read as contradictory to an implementer.
feasibilityConcerns: The runtime feature flag cannot be delivered as specified. §8 says 'Feature flag (runtime) | Read from /auth/me metadata'. backend/app/user_metadata.py:44-48 parse_user_metadata returns exactly {district, office_code, office_location} and drops every other key, and routes/auth.py:39 returns that object verbatim. Phase 0's rollout mechanism therefore requires a backend change that is in no B item — and per-user metadata is the wrong shape for the plan's stated 'per environment' gating anyway.

Phase 0 is costed at half its own component estimate. §11 gives Phase 0 ten days for AppShell (3.0) + labels (2.0) + Button set (2.0) + NextStepBanner (2.0) + FlowPage/ConfirmSheet (3.0) + BottomSheet (2.5) + ListDetail (2.0) + ResponsiveList (2.5) + EmptyState/Notice (1.0) + feature flag (1.0) = 21.0 component-days from §8, plus the Settings Account section. No team size or parallelism is stated anywhere in the plan, so the two numbers cannot be reconciled.

The §8 component table totals 53.5 days against a 66-day roadmap, leaving 12.5 days for the assembly of 19 page specs, 10 backend items, the 4-width × 3-theme × 7-role manual QA matrix, the axe route matrix, the VoiceOver walkthroughs, the device pass and the cross-client label mirroring — the three costs §11 says the other proposals omitted.

The AppShell layout-route migration is under-specified for a 3.0-day line. AppShell is currently called from 15 files (17 sites; MyWorkPage and MissionCenterProjectExplorer call it twice each), every call passes a `title` string and TerrainCrossSectionsPage passes `workspace` (which switches the shell to lg:h-screen lg:overflow-hidden). Moving to <Route element={<AppShell/>}> requires a per-route title/workspace mechanism (route handle or context) that the plan never names. AppShell also wraps all children in `product-card overflow-hidden`, which defeats position:sticky for the sticky indexes, sub-toolbars and action bars §6 relies on; it is not on the 'Delete on landing' list.

'For information (Consulted)' has no data source. §7.2 gives reviewers a Consulted group and §4 promises 'Consulted under For information, no buttons', but assessments.py:828 scopes the reviewer queue to `assignment_role IN ('REVIEWER','APPROVER')`, excluding CONSULTED. No B item adds it.

Verified deep-link breakage the plan misses: mobile/app/(tabs)/submissions/[id].tsx:5056 opens `${WEB_APP_URL}/submissions/{id}?section=terrain` (the only web path to the 3D scene from the app; the adjacent copy says 'The full interactive 3D scene opens in the WebUI'). SubmissionMeasurementContext.tsx:29-37 handles that param by scrolling to #terrain-3d-section — an anchor §7.6 deletes with the canvas. `?section=terrain` appears nowhere in §5.5 or the Phase 6 cross-client work.

Permission changes are made without being flagged as such. Today canEdit (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:162) is any FIELD_WORKER or ADMIN on a DRAFT/REJECTED submission — not assignment-scoped — and canReview (161) is the literal REVIEWER or ADMIN. §7.6 replaces both with isEngineer() + assessmentPermissions() and §4 scopes reviewers to 'assigned only'. That both widens (canonical GEOTECH_ENGINEER unblocked, correctly) and narrows (non-assigned engineers and legacy REVIEWER accounts lose access). The plan asserts the widening and is silent on the narrowing; whether the server already rejects the narrowed cases is unstated.

The 3D memory gate is inert on the primary field device: navigator.deviceMemory is not implemented in Safari/iPadOS, so `deviceMemory < 4` is false and a low-memory iPad passes the gate and loads the scene.

'One MapView mounted in the layout route and kept alive' (§7.14) conflicts with simultaneously-mounted maps: /incidents/:id/review renders a candidates map in a dialog over a case file that may be showing its site map, and §6.2 gives the desktop supporting pane its own Map tab. ArcGIS views cannot be shared across two mounted panes; whether embedded maps get their own views is not stated, and MapPanel is costed at 3.5 days.

The metric 'Requests to open a case: 6-8 -> 1' cannot hold on two of the three entry URLs. /assessments/:id and /submissions/:id must first resolve incident_id before they can call GET /incidents/{id}/case, so those are 2 requests; B3 does not say the endpoint accepts an assessment or submission id.

Several Home groups have no queue behind them. list_assessments exposes queue = office_chief | branch_chief | engineer | reviewer only. 'Reviewer needed' (assessments with no active REVIEWER), 'Ready to close out' (FINALIZED assessment + unresolved incident, scoped to the engineer), 'Recently accepted (7 d)' and 'Recently done by me' all need either new filters or client-side scans over the very limit:1000 fetches §11 says stay in place. Only B4 (Phase 5) touches this, three phases after Home ships.

Phase 3 lists its dependencies as '0, B1' although B1 lands in Phase 1 and Phase 3 also consumes Phase 1's NextStepBanner and the canEdit fix; the dependency graph understates the ordering constraint.
